HFT Arbitrage in Commodities

Commodities arbitrage has two regimes. Intra-exchange: fully hedged, favorable margin, and won on sub-microsecond latency. Inter-exchange: relative arbitrage, latency-sensitive, capital-intensive, held until mean reversion. How and why HFTs do both:

Intra-exchange

An underlying commodity on a futures exchange is more than a single contract. The full complex for a product includes:
  • Outright futures for >20 different expirations
  • Micro contracts with the same underlying but with smaller multipliers
  • Calendar spreads between outrights
  • Related intercommodity spreads

A futures exchange matching engine lists order books for all of these while also creating implied liquidity in both directions: implying spreads from outrights and implying outrights from spreads. Permutations of contracts and spreads present multiple arbitrage opportunities. Margin requirements for intra-exchange arbitrage trades are generally low given the offsets offered within

wrote a piece on compute capital markets, diving deep into factors that contribute to compute heterogeneity, current landscape, and how the sector can potentially grow over time
https://x.com/jinglingcookies/status/2081729288081199508

tweet.text:
Compute is a fundamental resource for the AI industry, powering training, post-training, inference and more in the AI pipeline.

Yet it's volatility, with H100 spot going from $8 to a range between $2 - $4 in just two years, has hardly been hedgeable. 

This is changing now. GPU-hours are becoming benchmarked, financialized, and traded, and this article explores the rise of the compute capital markets: who are the players, what's required for compute standardization and who will eventually dominate the market.
